questions.question: Let [latex] \{x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n\} [/latex] be a set of linearly independent vectors in [latex] \mathbb{R}^n [/latex]. questions.explanation: [latex]A_{ij}=x_i^Tx_j[/latex] is exactly the Gram matrix of the vectors [latex]x_1,\ldots,x_n[/latex]. A fundamental fact: the Gram matrix of a set of linearly independent vectors is always positive definite (strictly [latex]z^TAz>0[/latex] for every nonzero [latex]z[/latex], since [latex]z^TAz=\|\sum_iz_ix_i\|^2[/latex], which is zero only if the linear combination itself is zero — impossible for independent vectors and nonzero [latex]z[/latex]). A positive definite matrix has all strictly positive eigenvalues (and singular values), hence nonzero determinant and full rank — so [latex]A[/latex] is invertible . The other options (a zero singular value, zero determinant, or [latex]z^TAz=0[/latex] for some nonzero [latex]z[/latex]) are all impossible for a positive definite matrix. Answer: A is invertible Click Here for Detail Solution
